title: Duolingo CEO Luis von Ahn on AI, User Motivation, and Expanding Beyond Languages
excerpt: TIME spoke with Luis von Ahn about Duolingo’s story, user engagement, and how he’s approaching AI integration.
content_html:
When Luis von Ahn was 8 years old, growing up in Guatemala City, his mother bought him a computer. He was upset because he actually wanted a Nintendo, he recalls. “But you know, it changed my life because I learned how to use a computer.” Developing that skill eventually led to his creation of the educational app Duolingo, which is used by millions around the world to learn languages, and now other subjects, such as math and music. The company went public in 2021 and is currently valued at $5.7 billion. 

“Education has always been a big thing for me,” says von Ahn, 47. His mother, a doctor and single parent, didn’t earn much, but spent any spare money she had on ensuring von Ahn had access to the best education in Guatemala, he says. “The other kids in my neighborhood probably went to public school. It was very clear that I was years ahead of them in terms of what I was learning, and that always stuck with me,” he says. “And that's probably the biggest reason why we started Duolingo. The idea is to try to give education to everyone, regardless of whether you don't have a lot of money or you have a lot of money, you can use the same system.” Von Ahn believes the app has achieved that goal, and says its users range from across the socioeconomic spectrum. 

TIME spoke with von Ahn in May about Duolingo’s story, user engagement, and how he’s approaching AI integration. 

This conversation has been condensed and edited for clarity.

Tell me a bit about the evolution of Duolingo.

We started very small in 2011. We wanted to do something that would give equal access to education to everyone. At first, we didn't want to teach languages. At first, we thought we wanted to teach math, but we decided to teach languages, and the reason for that was because of English. In almost every country in the world, if you know English, you can make more money. There are a little under 2 billion people in the world learning English. Math has a billion people learning it. So English is basically the most learned subject that I know of in the whole world. So we thought, OK, let's do a thing that teaches languages for free. We launched it. It was very successful from the minute we launched it. It became the most downloaded app in the education category, and it has been since then. And we reached all kinds of really amazing numbers relatively early on. For example, at some point, there were more people learning languages on Duolingo in the U.S. than there are people learning languages across all U.S. high schools combined, and now that's true in most countries in the world. Not in every country—particularly in China, it's not yet true—but in most countries we teach more people languages than the public education system. So we're very proud of that. 

For the first four or five years, we made no money. We didn't have any ads. There was no subscription. Nothing. It was just free. Then we started monetizing around 2017, but one of the crazy things that happened is that we had hired all these people, and they had come to work at Duolingo to give free education. And when I said to everyone, we need to make money to sustain ourselves, there was a revolt. People did not want to—most of the employees were like, “Why? Why do we need to make money?” Which is crazy if you think about it, but I had to explain to them that you actually have to pay salaries, and that's how we have to make money, etc. But eventually, we found a good way to make money, which is our freemium model: everybody can use Duolingo entirely for free. But if you don't pay, you have to see some ads, and if you don't like ads, you can pay to subscribe, and it gets rid of the ads.

That worked, and then after that, we started at least being self-sustaining. At some point, we became profitable. We're now a publicly traded company, so we're very happy with that. The other thing that has happened over time is we've added more subjects. We started with just languages, but now we have math, music, and chess, and we're very happy with those. I'm particularly excited about math. I think over time, hopefully, it'll become almost as large as languages. Languages are much larger, but I'm hoping that math at some point will become as large as it.

Is English the most popular language? 

Yeah, for sure. Half of our users are learning English.

And where is it most used?

We have users in every single country in the world. The largest market is the U.S. in terms of number of users. Second is China, and then third [place] oscillates between Brazil, the U.K., and Germany. 

Are there complications to operating in China?

Yes. We're fine now, but China has a lot of regulation, and we have to go through that, but we're happy. China's not the number one fastest growing country, but it is relatively fast growing, and our expectation is that within one or two years China will be our largest market. It's just growing really fast. There's just a lot of people in China, also a lot of people who want to learn English. So you keep growing.

How many languages have you learned, or are you learning? 

I got pretty good at French to the point where I can watch TV shows in French. My pronunciation is not particularly good, but I can watch TV shows pretty well. I am currently learning Swedish because my wife is Swedish, and now Swedish is an excellent language. It just turns out not a particularly useful language to learn because all Swedes seem to know English. But I am learning it because my wife is Swedish. I'm not as good as I am at French.

I have to confess I don't use Duolingo, but I did speak to some friends who use it and got some feedback. A couple of things that I heard a few times were that they don't like the guilt-tripping constant reminders, and also the need to pay to progress… 

You don't need to pay to progress. You need to pay to turn off ads. And if you don't pay, you sort of cannot do too much per hour. That's basically it.

But there's also the AI function… 

Oh yeah, as in, you have to pay if you want to do the practicing conversation with AI. You have to pay because that also costs us money. Yeah.

I'm sure you hear similar feedback. How do you take that on board and how do you integrate that into improving the app?

Well, a couple of things. In terms of the guilt-tripping, we try a lot of things. The thing about learning something by yourself—and this is really what has made us the most popular education app in the world—the hardest thing about learning something by yourself is staying motivated. It's just really hard to stay motivated. Most people will tell you that they want to learn something, but their actions don't say the same thing. I mean, their actions are [that] they're going to go to Instagram or TikTok or whatever. One of the main things I've learned here at Duolingo over the last 15 years is what people say, what people do, and what people think—completely different things. So people will tell you they really want to learn something, etc. But it's very hard to stay motivated to learn something like a language. To learn a language to a relatively good point takes hundreds, if not thousands, of hours. That is just the case. There's no faster way to do that. Your brain needs that many hours to learn it. So we need to find ways to get people to continue doing it, and we just try everything we can. We try to make it fun. Try to make it as gamified as possible. We send you reminders. Some of the reminders are guilt-tripping, and it just turns out this works. And that's the idea. The idea is to try to get you to be motivated to continue working. I mean, learning.

It sounds like your workforce is very passionate…

Mission driven. Yes. 

There was a story about assessment of employees based on AI usage, which was rolled back. What happened and what did you learn from that experience?

Last year I sent a memo internally that, honestly internally it was not controversial. I mean, it was like, “Hey, we’ve got to use AI in as [many] places as we can.” There was one part that, at the time was not controversial, but we have since flipped, which is we're going to assess people's performance based on their use of AI. That's not going to be the only thing, but one of the things I look at is are you using AI or not? Because we really do believe that AI can make you a lot more productive. I sent that memo. Externally, people read that memo and thought that I was going to fire all our employees. This is actually not what happened. We didn't fire anybody. We in fact hired more employees last year, and part of the reason is it's just now an employee is way more valuable than before because one employee with AI can just do way more than a single employee before AI. So I want to keep hiring, but internally, what we learned over the last year was that there were people who did their job, and they had a lot of impact. But they're like, “AI doesn't really apply to my job. Do you want me to just use AI for no reason?” And they had very good arguments. So, we've gone back to just, your performance is based on the impact you have on the company, regardless of what you do. So yeah, we shouldn't have done that, but we did.

You talked about offering something to users that isn't Instagram or TikTok. There are people who are also thinking about how they use AI and even not wanting to use it. How do you balance improving the app using AI integration against keeping those loyal users who like using Duolingo because it's not social media or ChatGPT?

Ultimately, our goal is to teach you things that take a long time to learn. That's our goal. It turns out AI can really help us teach you those things much better. A really good example is conversational practice. Before AI, there was no way for you to practice conversation on Duolingo, and the only way we could have done it before AI was to pair you up with another human. But this is one of those cases where people say they want to talk to another human in a language that they are not comfortable with, but people do not actually talk to another human in a language that they're not comfortable with. We tried many times. I believe about 5% of humanity's population is willing to do that, and the other 90% to 95% doesn't actually want to. Even though they say they do, they don't actually want to do that because it just requires too much. People are ashamed. Before AI, we simply could not get you to practice conversation. It just was a hole in your learning. Now with AI, you can actually fully practice conversation, and that you learn the language better. So, for our usage of AI, we have this golden rule internally in the company, which is we are only going to use AI for the benefit of our learners, and so that's it. In fact, the overwhelming majority of our usage of AI is either in speeding up our development process or in teaching better. And so, I understand that some people may not love using ChatGPT, etc. But you know, ultimately, we're just trying to teach you better.

Then we started monetizing around 2017, but one of the crazy things that happened is that we had hired all these people, and they had come to work at Duolingo to give free education. And when I said to everyone, we need to make money to sustain ourselves, there was a revolt. People did not want to—most of the employees were like, “Why? Why do we need to make money?” Which is crazy if you think about it, but I had to explain to them that you actually have to pay salaries, and that's how we have to make money, etc. But eventually, we found a good way to make money, which is our freemium model: everybody can use Duolingo entirely for free. But if you don't pay, you have to see some ads, and if you don't like ads, you can pay to subscribe, and it gets rid of the ads.

blocks.html_en: Well, a couple of things. In terms of the guilt-tripping, we try a lot of things. The thing about learning something by yourself—and this is really what has made us the most popular education app in the world—the hardest thing about learning something by yourself is staying motivated. It's just really hard to stay motivated. Most people will tell you that they want to learn something, but their actions don't say the same thing. I mean, their actions are [that] they're going to go to Instagram or TikTok or whatever. One of the main things I've learned here at Duolingo over the last 15 years is what people say, what people do, and what people think—completely different things. So people will tell you they really want to learn something, etc. But it's very hard to stay motivated to learn something like a language. To learn a language to a relatively good point takes hundreds, if not thousands, of hours. That is just the case. There's no faster way to do that. Your brain needs that many hours to learn it. So we need to find ways to get people to continue doing it, and we just try everything we can. We try to make it fun. Try to make it as gamified as possible. We send you reminders. Some of the reminders are guilt-tripping, and it just turns out this works. And that's the idea. The idea is to try to get you to be motivated to continue working. I mean, learning.

blocks.html_en: There was a story about assessment of employees based on AI usage, which was rolled back. What happened and what did you learn from that experience?

sentences.en: There was a story about assessment of employees based on AI usage, which was rolled back.
sentences.zh: 有一个关于根据人工智能使用情况对员工进行评估的故事，该故事已被撤回。

sentences.en: What happened and what did you learn from that experience?
sentences.zh: 发生了什么？您从这次经历中学到了什么？

blocks.html_en: Last year I sent a memo internally that, honestly internally it was not controversial. I mean, it was like, “Hey, we’ve got to use AI in as [many] places as we can.” There was one part that, at the time was not controversial, but we have since flipped, which is we're going to assess people's performance based on their use of AI. That's not going to be the only thing, but one of the things I look at is are you using AI or not? Because we really do believe that AI can make you a lot more productive. I sent that memo. Externally, people read that memo and thought that I was going to fire all our employees. This is actually not what happened. We didn't fire anybody. We in fact hired more employees last year, and part of the reason is it's just now an employee is way more valuable than before because one employee with AI can just do way more than a single employee before AI. So I want to keep hiring, but internally, what we learned over the last year was that there were people who did their job, and they had a lot of impact. But they're like, “AI doesn't really apply to my job. Do you want me to just use AI for no reason?” And they had very good arguments. So, we've gone back to just, your performance is based on the impact you have on the company, regardless of what you do. So yeah, we shouldn't have done that, but we did.

blocks.html_en: You talked about offering something to users that isn't Instagram or TikTok. There are people who are also thinking about how they use AI and even not wanting to use it. How do you balance improving the app using AI integration against keeping those loyal users who like using Duolingo because it's not social media or ChatGPT?

sentences.en: You talked about offering something to users that isn't Instagram or TikTok.
sentences.zh: 您谈到向 Instagram 或 TikTok 以外的用户提供一些东西。

sentences.en: How do you balance improving the app using AI integration against keeping those loyal users who like using Duolingo because it's not social media or ChatGPT?
sentences.zh: 您如何平衡使用 AI 集成改进应用程序和保留那些因为 Duolingo 不是社交媒体或 ChatGPT 而喜欢使用 Duolingo 的忠实用户？

blocks.html_en: Ultimately, our goal is to teach you things that take a long time to learn. That's our goal. It turns out AI can really help us teach you those things much better. A really good example is conversational practice. Before AI, there was no way for you to practice conversation on Duolingo, and the only way we could have done it before AI was to pair you up with another human. But this is one of those cases where people say they want to talk to another human in a language that they are not comfortable with, but people do not actually talk to another human in a language that they're not comfortable with. We tried many times. I believe about 5% of humanity's population is willing to do that, and the other 90% to 95% doesn't actually want to. Even though they say they do, they don't actually want to do that because it just requires too much. People are ashamed. Before AI, we simply could not get you to practice conversation. It just was a hole in your learning. Now with AI, you can actually fully practice conversation, and that you learn the language better. So, for our usage of AI, we have this golden rule internally in the company, which is we are only going to use AI for the benefit of our learners, and so that's it. In fact, the overwhelming majority of our usage of AI is either in speeding up our development process or in teaching better. And so, I understand that some people may not love using ChatGPT, etc. But you know, ultimately, we're just trying to teach you better.

sentences.zh: 我们尝试了很多次。

sentences.en: I believe about 5% of humanity's population is willing to do that, and the other 90% to 95% doesn't actually want to.
sentences.zh: 我相信大约有 5% 的人类愿意这样做，而另外 90% 到 95% 的人实际上并不愿意这样做。

sentences.en: Even though they say they do, they don't actually want to do that because it just requires too much.
sentences.zh: 尽管他们嘴上说愿意，但实际上他们并不想这样做，因为这要求太多。

sentences.en: People are ashamed.
sentences.zh: 人们感到羞愧。

sentences.en: Before AI, we simply could not get you to practice conversation.
sentences.zh: 在人工智能出现之前，我们根本无法让你练习对话。

sentences.en: It just was a hole in your learning.
sentences.zh: 这只是你学习中的一个漏洞。

sentences.en: Now with AI, you can actually fully practice conversation, and that you learn the language better.
sentences.zh: 现在有了人工智能，你实际上可以充分练习对话，并且可以更好地学习语言。

sentences.en: So, for our usage of AI, we have this golden rule internally in the company, which is we are only going to use AI for the benefit of our learners, and so that's it.
sentences.zh: 因此，对于我们对人工智能的使用，我们在公司内部有一条黄金法则，那就是我们只会为了学习者的利益而使用人工智能，仅此而已。

sentences.en: In fact, the overwhelming majority of our usage of AI is either in speeding up our development process or in teaching better.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我们对人工智能的绝大多数使用要么是为了加快我们的开发过程，要么是为了更好地教学。

sentences.en: And so, I understand that some people may not love using ChatGPT, etc. But you know, ultimately, we're just trying to teach you better.
sentences.zh: 因此，我理解有些人可能不喜欢使用 ChatGPT 等。但你知道，最终，我们只是想更好地教你。

content_html_zh:
路易斯·冯·安 (Luis von Ahn) 在危地马拉城长大，8 岁时，他的母亲给他买了一台电脑。 他回忆道，他很沮丧，因为他实际上想要一台任天堂。 “但你知道，它改变了我的生活，因为我学会了如何使用电脑。” 开发这种技能最终导致他创建了教育应用程序 Duolingo，全世界数百万人使用该应用程序来学习语言，现在还学习其他科目，例如数学和音乐。 该公司于2021年上市，目前估值为57亿美元。

“教育对我来说一直是一件大事，”47 岁的冯·安 (von Ahn) 说。 他说，他的母亲是一名医生和单亲妈妈，收入不多，但她把所有的闲钱都花在了确保冯·安获得危地马拉最好的教育上。 “我家附近的其他孩子可能都上公立学校。 很明显，就我所学的知识而言，我比他们领先很多年，而且这一点一直困扰着我，”他说。 “这可能是我们创办 Duolingo 的最大原因。 我们的想法是尝试为每个人提供教育，无论你是没有很多钱还是有很多钱，你都可以使用相同的系统。” 冯·安 (Von Ahn) 相信该应用程序已经实现了这一目标，并表示其用户涵盖各个社会经济领域。

5 月份，《时代》杂志采访了冯·安 (von Ahn)，谈论了 Duolingo 的故事、用户参与度以及他如何实现人工智能集成。

为了清晰起见，本次对话经过精简和编辑。

请告诉我一些有关 Duolingo 的演变的信息。

我们从 2011 年开始规模很小。 我们想做一些事情，让每个人都有平等的受教育机会。 起初，我们不想教语言。 起初，我们以为我们想教数学，但我们决定教语言，原因是英语。 在世界上几乎每个国家，如果你懂英语，你就能赚更多钱。 世界上有不到 20 亿人在学习英语。 有十亿人在学习数学。 所以英语基本上是我所知道的全世界最学得的学科。 所以我们想，好吧，让我们做一件免费教授语言的事情吧。 我们推出了它。 从我们推出它的那一刻起，它就非常成功。 它成为教育类别中下载次数最多的应用程序，从那时起一直如此。 我们很早就达到了各种非常惊人的数字。 例如，在某个时候，美国在 Duolingo 上学习语言的人数比美国所有高中学习语言的人数总和还要多，现在世界上大多数国家都是如此。 并非在每个国家——尤其是在中国，情况还不是如此——但在大多数国家，我们教授的语言数量多于公共教育系统。 所以我们对此感到非常自豪。

最初四五年，我们没赚到钱。 我们没有任何广告。 没有订阅。 没有什么。 它只是免费的。 然后我们在 2017 年左右开始盈利，但发生的一件疯狂的事情是我们雇佣了所有这些人，他们来到 Duolingo 工作来提供免费教育。 当我对每个人说，我们需要赚钱来养活自己时，出现了反抗。 人们不想这样做——大多数员工都会说，“为什么？ 我们为什么要赚钱？” 如果你仔细想想，这很疯狂，但我不得不向他们解释，你实际上必须支付工资，这就是我们必须赚钱的方式，等等。但最终，我们找到了一个赚钱的好方法，这就是我们的免费增值模式：每个人都可以完全免费使用 Duolingo。 但如果你不付费，你就必须看到一些广告，如果你不喜欢广告，你可以付费订阅，它就摆脱了广告。

这奏效了，在那之后，我们至少开始自给自足。 在某个时候，我们开始盈利。 我们现在是一家上市公司，因此我们对此感到非常高兴。 随着时间的推移发生的另一件事是我们添加了更多主题。 我们一开始只学习语言，但现在我们有了数学、音乐和国际象棋，我们对这些感到非常满意。 我对数学特别感兴趣。 我认为随着时间的推移，希望它会变得几乎和语言一样大。 语言要大得多，但我希望数学在某个时候也能变得和它一样大。

英语是最流行的语言吗？

是的，当然。 我们一半的用户正在学习英语。

它在哪里使用最多？

我们在世界每个国家都有用户。 就用户数量而言，最大的市场是美国。 第二名是中国，第三名在巴西、英国和德国之间摇摆不定。

在中国经营有困难吗？

是的。 我们现在很好，但中国有很多监管，我们必须经历这些，但我们很高兴。 中国不是增长最快的国家，但增长相对较快，我们预计在一两年内中国将成为我们最大的市场。 它增长得非常快。 中国有很多人，也有很多人想学英语。 所以你不断成长。

您已经学习或正在学习多少种语言？

我的法语相当不错，可以看法语电视节目。 我的发音不是特别好，但是我可以很好地看电视节目。 我目前正在学习瑞典语，因为我的妻子是瑞典人，现在瑞典语是一门很好的语言。 事实证明，这并不是一种特别有用的语言，因为所有瑞典人似乎都懂英语。 但我正在学习它，因为我的妻子是瑞典人。 我的法语不太好。

我必须承认我不使用 Duolingo，但我确实与一些使用它的朋友交谈并得到了一些反馈。 我多次听到的一些事情是，他们不喜欢令人内疚的不断提醒，也不喜欢为了进步而付出代价……

您无需付费即可取得进步。 您需要付费才能关闭广告。 如果你不付钱，你每小时就不能做太多事情。 基本上就是这样。

但还有人工智能功能……

哦，是的，如果你想与人工智能练习对话，你就必须付费。 您必须付费，因为这也会花费我们的钱。 是的。

我相信您也听到过类似的反馈。 您如何考虑这一点以及如何将其整合到改进应用程序中？

嗯，有几件事。 就内疚感而言，我们尝试了很多事情。 自学的最难之处在于保持动力，而这正是我们成为世界上最受欢迎的教育应用程序的真正原因。 保持动力真的很难。 大多数人会告诉你他们想学习一些东西，但他们的行为并没有表达同样的意思。 我的意思是，他们的行为是他们会去 Instagram 或 TikTok 或其他什么网站。 过去 15 年里，我在 Duolingo 学到的主要事情之一是人们所说的、人们所做的和人们所想的——完全不同的事情。 所以人们会告诉你他们真的想学一些东西等等。但是很难保持学习语言之类的东西的动力。 将一门语言学习到相对较好的程度需要数百甚至数千个小时。 事实就是如此。 没有更快的方法可以做到这一点。 你的大脑需要很多时间来学习它。 所以我们需要找到方法让人们继续这样做，我们只是尽我们所能。 我们努力让它变得有趣。 尝试使其尽可能游戏化。 我们向您发送提醒。 有些提醒会让人感到内疚，但事实证明这是有效的。 这就是我们的想法。 这个想法是试图让你有动力继续工作。 我的意思是，学习。

听起来你们的员工非常热情……

使命驱动。 是的。

有一个关于根据人工智能使用情况对员工进行评估的故事，该故事已被撤回。 发生了什么？您从这次经历中学到了什么？

去年我在内部发送了一份备忘录，说实话，在内部这并没有争议。 我的意思是，就像是，“嘿，我们必须在尽可能多的地方使用人工智能。” 有一个部分当时并没有争议，但后来我们改变了主意，那就是我们将根据人们对人工智能的使用来评估他们的表现。 这不是唯一的事情，但我关注的事情之一是你是否使用人工智能？ 因为我们确实相信人工智能可以提高您的工作效率。 我发送了那份备忘录。 在外部，人们读了这份备忘录并认为我要解雇所有员工。 这实际上并不是发生的事情。 我们没有解雇任何人。 事实上，我们去年雇佣了更多的员工，部分原因是现在员工比以前更有价值，因为一名拥有人工智能的员工可以比人工智能之前的一名员工做更多的事情。 所以我想继续招聘，但在内部，我们去年学到的是，有些人做好了自己的工作，而且产生了很大的影响。 但他们会说，“人工智能并不真正适用于我的工作。 你想让我无缘无故地使用人工智能吗？” 他们有很好的论据。 所以，我们回到了刚才的观点，你的表现取决于你对公司的影响，无论你做什么。 所以，是的，我们不应该这样做，但我们做到了。

您谈到向 Instagram 或 TikTok 以外的用户提供一些东西。 还有一些人也在思考如何使用人工智能，甚至不想使用它。 您如何平衡使用 AI 集成改进应用程序和保留那些因为 Duolingo 不是社交媒体或 ChatGPT 而喜欢使用 Duolingo 的忠实用户？

最终，我们的目标是教给您需要很长时间才能学习的东西。 这就是我们的目标。 事实证明，人工智能确实可以帮助我们更好地教你这些东西。 一个很好的例子是会话练习。 在人工智能出现之前，你无法在 Duolingo 上练习对话，而在人工智能出现之前，我们唯一能做到的方法就是将你与另一个人配对。 但这是一种情况，人们说他们想用他们不舒服的语言与另一个人交谈，但人们实际上并没有用他们不舒服的语言与另一个人交谈。 我们尝试了很多次。 我相信大约有 5% 的人类愿意这样做，而另外 90% 到 95% 的人实际上并不愿意这样做。 尽管他们嘴上说愿意，但实际上他们并不想这样做，因为这要求太多。 人们感到羞愧。 在人工智能出现之前，我们根本无法让你练习对话。 这只是你学习中的一个漏洞。 现在有了人工智能，你实际上可以充分练习对话，并且可以更好地学习语言。 因此，对于我们对人工智能的使用，我们在公司内部有一条黄金法则，那就是我们只会为了学习者的利益而使用人工智能，仅此而已。 事实上，我们对人工智能的绝大多数使用要么是为了加快我们的开发过程，要么是为了更好地教学。 因此，我理解有些人可能不喜欢使用 ChatGPT 等。但你知道，最终，我们只是想更好地教你。
